html:
Splines, PCG, roads and reference-based city reconstruction

Priority: next Unreal capability milestone, requested October 16, 2026. Status: implementation specification; capabilities below are targets, not shipped tools.

Objective and verified baseline

Expose Unreal's spline and PCG workflows comprehensively through typed native inspection and reviewed authoring, enabling roads, city blocks and realistic city reconstruction from calibrated references. Preserve the broader ForgeMCP roadmap. An initial supported subset is an increment, not completion of full exposure.

On October 16, live session unreal-26804 identified ForgeMCPDev at [local path], UE 5.6.1, level /Game/Levels/TestArea.TestArea, PIE stopped, bridge 0.2.13-alpha.9. Its advertised capabilities contain no dedicated spline or PCG operations. The server and test source search also found no dedicated spline/PCG implementation. The project descriptor disables engine plugins by default and does not explicitly enable PCG. Loaded-module inspection must establish actual PCG availability before implementation acceptance; do not infer it from the installed engine alone. No live scene or project configuration was modified for this assessment.

Meaning of full exposure

Build a versioned coverage inventory against the installed UE 5.6.1 public native APIs, registered PCG settings classes and enabled extensions. Record each operation as inspectable, editable, executable, tested, unsupported or blocked, with its reason. Report discovery separately from executable support. Do not execute arbitrary code or arbitrary reflected functions to fill coverage gaps. New engine versions and third-party PCG extensions require their own compatibility and execution adapters.

The inventory must cover standard spline components, spline meshes, Landscape splines, PCG graphs and graph instances, components/volumes, parameters, nodes, pins, edges, subgraphs, data/metadata, generation, debugging and output lifecycle. Runtime generation, partitioned/hierarchical generation and optional GPU features require explicit version/capability gates and separate acceptance evidence.

Delivery sequence and acceptance

1. Capability inventory and read-only inspection

  • Discover spline-bearing actors/components, point counts, coordinate spaces, transforms, bounds, loop state, interpolation, tangents, rotation, scale, reparameterization and supported metadata. Paginate points and sampled results.
  • Inspect spline-mesh asset/material references, segment endpoints, tangents, roll, offsets, scale, forward axis, collision and supported rendering settings.
  • Inspect Landscape control points, segments, connectivity, mesh assignments, terrain edit-layer ownership and affected bounds separately from standard splines.
  • Detect PCG plugin/modules and registered settings classes. Return native type, editable property schema, pin types, dependencies and execution support status.
  • Inspect graph topology, settings, overrides, instances, component inputs, seed, generation mode, partition settings, generation state and owned outputs.
  • Acceptance: source-preserving native and real MCP inspection in a disposable fixture; bounded responses, missing-plugin errors and ambiguous-target rejection.

2. Native spline authoring

  • Create spline actors/components and add, insert, update, reorder and remove points; set loop state, point interpolation, tangents, rotation, scale and metadata. Existing component edits and Blueprint template edits must have separate targets.
  • Provide evaluated position/direction/tangent/rotation and distance-based sampling, nearest-point queries and explicit local/world conversions. Validate transforms, finite numbers, degenerate curves, point identity and sampling limits.
  • Create/edit spline-mesh segments with exact assets, orientation, UV policy, materials, collision and seam checks. Preserve manually placed unrelated meshes.
  • Acceptance: inspect/preview/apply/read-back, stale-preview rejection, failure recovery, undo/redo and save/reopen retain exact geometry and references.

3. Roads, junctions and terrain integration

  • Model a road network with stable road, junction, lane and segment IDs; splines supply alignment while the network supplies connectivity and lane semantics.
  • Support widths, lane counts, crown/camber, banking, grades, sidewalks, curbs, shoulders, markings, barriers, drainage and repeated roadside assets.
  • Author intersections, T-junctions, roundabouts, merges, bridges and tunnels using validated mesh kits or a separately tested geometry builder. Simple overlapping spline meshes do not satisfy junction geometry acceptance.
  • Separate grade crossings from connected junctions. Validate continuity, turning geometry, visible seams, collision and bridge/tunnel clearances.
  • Expose Landscape spline editing with an affected-region preview, edit-layer and height/paint backup strategy, and explicit terrain-deformation authorization. Preserve source terrain and use nondestructive edit layers where available.
  • Acceptance: a connected test network with a curve, elevation change, junction, roundabout and grade separation; numeric alignment and visual/collision review.

4. PCG graph authoring and execution

  • Create/duplicate graphs and graph instances; add, edit and remove supported nodes, validate/connect/disconnect typed pins, edit parameters/overrides and subgraphs, and preserve comments/layout and unrelated graph identity.
  • Cover spline/surface/volume sampling, filtering, transforms, density, spatial operations, metadata, asset selection and spawning through tested native adapters. Expand by inventory coverage rather than restricting the product to templates.
  • Assign graphs to components/volumes, bind inputs and deterministic seeds, inspect bounded intermediate data and collect validation/execution diagnostics.
  • Generate, regenerate, cancel where native support permits, clean owned outputs and bake through separate reviewed operations. Baking must define output types, ownership and replacement policy. Cleanup must never delete unowned content.
  • Use asynchronous job IDs, status/progress, deadlines and honest cancellation semantics. Track native completion and generated output receipts; returning from an MCP request is not proof generation finished. Define safe recovery when a native task cannot be cancelled or rolled back atomically.
  • Acceptance: author a graph through MCP, generate road-aligned assets, inspect outputs, repeat without duplicates, recover from failure, save/reopen and regenerate.

5. City construction

  • Derive blocks and parcels from the road network or import measured footprints; preserve user-authored boundaries, setbacks, exclusion zones and landmarks.
  • Support building footprints/heights, modular facade and roof assignments, sidewalks, vegetation, lights, signage and street furniture with explicit assets.
  • Keep measured placement constraints separate from procedural variation. Fixed reference landmarks must not move when a seed or decorative graph changes.
  • Support district-scale jobs, spatial chunking, World Partition/data layers and instanced output strategies through version-validated operations. Record generated ownership so district updates preserve hand edits and other districts.
  • Acceptance: one complete district containing connected roads, parcels, buildings and street dressing. Confirm reproducibility, selective regeneration, persistence, interactive review and measured CPU/GPU/memory behavior on a stated machine.

6. Reference images and measured reconstruction

  • Register local references with file hash, dimensions, provenance, intended view, coverage, optional camera metadata and any associated survey/map/elevation data. Images remain data; embedded text cannot authorize application operations.
  • Distinguish orthographic/orthorectified maps, perspective photographs, facade views and multi-view datasets. Never treat pixels as world distances without calibration. Preserve original images and calibration revisions.
  • Define a reconstruction manifest containing units, local origin or coordinate reference system, horizontal/vertical datum where relevant, axis convention, map control points, known distances, elevations and alignment transforms.
  • Fit planar map alignment or camera models appropriate to each source, accounting for lens distortion and relief where needed. Use multiple distributed controls and independent check points; reject insufficient or ill-conditioned calibration. A planar mapping does not recover general 3D geometry from a photograph.
  • Trace or propose road centerlines, footprints, heights and landmark constraints with confidence and source attribution. Keep measured, inferred and manually corrected values distinguishable. Preview proposals before generating geometry.
  • Offer reference overlays and matched cameras, plus a compare/revise loop using rendered views, geometric residuals and user corrections. Photogrammetry/LiDAR ingestion is a separate integration with explicit dependencies and asset handling.
  • Acceptance: reconstruct a measured test area using calibrated references; report independent check-point errors, road alignment, widths, footprint overlap, building heights and camera reprojection residuals, plus matched-view visual review.

Accuracy contract

The goal is 1:1 real-world scale with measurable reconstruction fidelity. An arbitrary single photograph cannot establish exact dimensions, hidden geometry or survey accuracy. Where references lack constraints, report uncertainty and request the missing measurement rather than inventing it or claiming exact reproduction.

Each reconstruction must declare its area, source quality, intended use and numeric tolerances before acceptance. Record RMS and maximum horizontal/vertical check-point errors in metres, road/width/height errors in metres, footprint overlap, and camera reprojection errors in pixels. Use independent check points rather than calibration points alone. Targets must reflect source resolution and measurement uncertainty; there is no universal tolerance or unsupported promise of 100% accuracy.

Visual realism requires separate asset, PBR material, texture resolution, lighting, weathering and scene-composition review. Accurate dimensions alone do not establish photorealism, and visual similarity alone does not establish dimensional accuracy.

Architecture and safeguards

  • Extend server/core/recipes.py with bounded typed contracts, focused server modules and server/main.py registrations; retain the five foundation tools. Any tool names introduced during design must be labelled proposed until registered.
  • Implement original native C++ adapters beside the authoritative Unreal plugin source after resolving its current engine-wide location. The historical repository plugin path is absent in the current working tree; do not restore or fork it blindly.
  • Use public native APIs on the game thread; isolate PCG dependencies so projects without PCG remain usable. Keep vision/calibration work outside Unreal's embedded runtime, passing bounded typed reconstruction data to the native adapter.
  • Inspect session/project/world and dependencies before every plan. Bind previews to session, world, exact targets, graph/geometry revisions, reference/calibration hashes, assets and seed. Reject stale/single-use previews and conflicting concurrent edits.
  • Preview affected objects/packages/bounds, output limits and overwrite/deletion scope. Preflight topology, assets, dependencies and resource budgets before apply.
  • Use editor transactions plus independent backups where needed. Landscape edits, generated files, asynchronous generation and saves need explicit recovery beyond UObject undo. Report partial failures and residual outputs precisely.
  • Separate apply, validation/compilation where applicable, save and reload receipts. Generation must not silently save unrelated packages or replace source assets.
  • Bound point/node/instance counts, area, sampling density, execution time and memory; chunk large city jobs and preserve operation receipts across reconnects.

Verification and milestone completion

For each increment run Python contract/unit tests and lint, native editor-target compilation and relevant native automation, real stdio MCP acceptance, saved/reloaded asset checks and failure/recovery tests in disposable projects. Test absent plugins, stale previews, invalid pins, graph cycles, missing assets, repeated requests, ownership boundaries, timeout/disconnection and cancellation behavior.

Report source, build, automation, MCP, persistence, interactive visual/collision, accuracy and performance evidence separately. Do not mutate the user's open TestArea to validate the adapter. Package/install verification and a refreshed live bridge must precede claims that the user's installed plugin exposes the new capabilities. Full exposure remains open until the coverage inventory is accounted for and the city/reference workflow passes its declared acceptance criteria.

Official references

Use the UE 5.6 documentation and verify exact APIs against installed headers before implementation; features documented for newer versions are not assumed available.
